preset_sofa_prompt: Create a low, wide mid-century sofa with two deep rectangular seat cushions in olive velvet. Keep the back lower than the arms are long and curve it gently around both ends. Wrap that continuous back and both outward-sweeping arms in the same olive fabric. Show a narrow warm-gold piping line along the top edge of each seat cushion. Support the sofa on exactly four tapered walnut legs, angled slightly outward and mounted just inside the corners. Leave an open shadow gap beneath the upholstered frame. Use softly rounded edges, a matte fabric finish, and slightly satin wood. Show the sofa alone as one static prop, without throw pillows or a room.
preset_bed_prompt: Create a double bed with a low rectangular honey-oak platform, a thick ivory mattress, and a taller softly arched oak headboard. The mattress should sit inside the platform with a slim oak border showing on both sides and at the foot. Put two cream pillows side by side against the headboard and a folded dusty-blue blanket across the lower third of the mattress. Fit exactly two drawers into the platform, one per long side, with recessed dark-bronze pulls. The drawers should sit flush with the outer frame. Use satin oak, soft fabric, and a gently beveled frame. Keep the bed freestanding and leave out a room, nightstands, and other furniture.
preset_microscope_prompt: Create a compact portable microscope for a field laboratory. Use a low charcoal horseshoe base and a single curved cream-enamel support rising at the rear. Mount a short angled black eyepiece at the top and a brushed-steel turret with exactly three dark objective barrels underneath it. Place a thin rectangular black stage directly below the turret, with a centered round light opening and two silver slide clips. Add one knurled focus wheel to each side of the support, sharing the same horizontal axis. Place a small teal power switch near the front right of the base. Keep the whole instrument grounded and static, with clean enamel, dark rubber grips, and satin metal.
preset_radio_prompt: Create a compact field radio with a thick rounded rectangular case, slightly taller than it is deep. Make the body mustard-yellow painted metal with charcoal rubber corner bumpers. On the front, put a circular black speaker grille on the left and a narrow dark-green tuning window on the right, above two small knurled black knobs. Use a row of simple pale tick marks in the window. Attach a short silver telescoping antenna at the rear right and a curved charcoal carrying handle across the top with two metal mounts. Put a shallow battery cover on the back. Give the case softened edges and subtle wear at the corners. Make it one static prop with no loose cable.
preset_winch_prompt: Create a heavy deck-mounted cargo winch with a broad rectangular slate-blue steel base. Set a horizontal cable drum between two upright steel supports. Make the drum dark steel with thick round flanges and several visible neat turns of braided gray cable. Mount a short ribbed teal electric motor to the right support, aligned with the drum shaft. Run one loose end of the cable forward through two guide rollers to a single yellow hook resting against the base. Add four dark bolt heads at the base corners and a small orange service plate on the motor housing. Use worn painted steel and restrained satin highlights. Show only the static winch and its attached parts.
preset_valve_prompt: Create a freestanding industrial shutoff valve with a squat dark-blue cast-iron body and two horizontal pipe ends on the same axis. Finish each pipe end with a broad circular flange and six evenly spaced steel bolt heads. Rise from the center of the body with a short silver stem and cap it with a bright red four-spoke handwheel lying flat above the valve. Add a small brass identification plate to the front of the body, with a plain inset rectangle for later labeling. Use rough cast iron, matte red enamel, and darker steel at the joins. Show the complete assembly as a static component without a floor, pipes extending beyond the flanges, or machinery around it.
preset_doorway_prompt: Create a modular stone doorway for a dungeon wall. The rectangular module should be taller than it is wide, with a broad rounded arch above a clear opening. Build the sides from staggered gray limestone blocks and make the arch from wedge-shaped stones with a larger central keystone. Set a thin black iron liner just inside the stone opening and a worn slate threshold across the bottom. Give the blocks broad bevels and a few larger chips near the base, keeping the rear face flat so it can meet another wall piece. Use muted grays with a little moss-green staining low down. Keep the opening empty and supply only the doorway module.
preset_stall_prompt: Create a small open-front market stall as one grouped scenery prop. Use four warm timber posts on a broad rectangular counter base, with a peaked canopy overhead. Give the canopy alternating wide terracotta and cream cloth panels, draped slightly at the front edge. Put two shallow wooden produce trays on the left side of the counter, with simplified green and orange fruit. Leave the right side clear and place a single dark wooden crate underneath it. Brace the posts with short diagonals and make the counter front from horizontal wood planks. Use matte cloth and slightly worn timber. Keep the stall static and self-contained, without a street, signs, or people.
preset_lantern_prompt: Create a compact ship lantern with a broad round aged-brass base and a tapered cap, joined by exactly four curved brass cage ribs. Fit a pale amber glass cylinder inside the ribs and give its center a gentle amber glow. Add a short black hanging loop centered on the top and a shallow circular foot underneath so the lantern can sit on a deck. Place a small hinged brass access panel with one dark latch on the front of the base. Use satin brass with darker joints and broad glass surfaces that read clearly from a distance. Keep the silhouette compact and show a single static lantern without a chain, deck, or background objects.
preset_crate_prompt: Create a compact sci-fi supply crate with a low rectangular body, a flat lid, and clipped vertical corners. Use matte olive-green painted panels and thick charcoal corner guards that wrap from the sides onto the lid. Mount exactly two orange latches on the front, evenly spaced across the seam. Recess one dark carry handle into each short end. Add three broad reinforcing ribs across the top and a small blank ivory label plate between the front latches. Keep the base flat and the lid closed. Show clean joins and chunky game-readable details with a little edge wear. Supply one static crate without tools, contents, or nearby scenery.
preset_rover_prompt: Create a small four-wheel utility rover for carrying equipment across rocky terrain. Use a short, wide chassis, high ground clearance, and four equally sized charcoal tires with simple chunky tread. Put a compact cream-colored enclosed cab above the front axle, with a broad blue-gray windshield and one side window on each side. Behind it, fit a low open cargo bed with olive metal side rails and a closed tailgate. Add a dark bumper and two round pale headlights to the front. Keep the wheels straight and evenly spaced and the entire rover level at rest. Use matte painted panels and satin metal railings, with no driver, cargo, or terrain.
preset_rowboat_prompt: Create a small open wooden rowboat with a pointed bow, a flat stern transom, and a broad shallow hull that narrows at both ends. Make the outer hull muted teal painted timber with a dark wood rim following the full top edge. Inside, show a plain honey-brown floor and exactly two lighter wooden benches spanning across the hull. Mount a small metal oarlock on each side beside the forward bench. Lay two wooden oars side by side along the inside floor, with their broad blades toward the stern. Use subdued weathering on the paint and satin wood inside. Show the boat alone without water, dock, figures, or an added stand.
translation_precision_hint: Qwen3.5-9B-Heretic translates your description. If you’re unsure, choose Q4. This choice is separate from CCORE’s asset-generation model.
translation_q4_help: About 5.8 GB of weights, plus working memory. Uses lower-precision weights to reduce GPU memory use.
translation_q8_help: About 9.8 GB of weights, plus working memory. Keeps more numerical precision and needs more VRAM; translation quality is not guaranteed to improve.
translation_gpu_only: Both options run on the GPU. If the selected model will not fit, free GPU memory or choose Q4. Foundry will keep your description and will not silently switch to CPU offloading.
translation_invalid_precision: Choose Q4 or Q8 for translation.
